title: Development of the Kidney - Embryology Lecture
department_desc: Anatomy and embryonic development of the kidneys, ureters, bladder and urethra
matrix_title: Twisted Medicine High-Yield Pearls: Development of the Kidney - Embryology Lecture

summary_table.content: High-Yield Embryological Milestones, Derivatives & Board Pearls

• Pronephros: Early week 4 (cervical); completely non-functional in humans; full regression by end week 4. • Mesonephros: Late week 4-10 (thoracolumbar); produces primitive dilute urine; Wolffian duct persists in males (epididymis, vas deferens, ejaculatory duct, seminal vesicles). • Metanephros: Week 5 onward (sacral S1-S2); permanent kidney; urine filtration starts at Week 12. • Ureteric Bud (Collecting System): Outgrowth of caudal Wolffian duct -> Ureter, Renal Pelvis, Major Calyces (2-3), Minor Calyces (8-18),

Collecting Ducts & Tubules (1-3 million). • Metanephric Blastema (Excretory Nephrons): Sacral intermediate mesoderm -> Bowman's Capsule, PCT, Loop of Henle, DCT. • Critical Junction: DCT (blastema) connects to Collecting Tubule (bud). Failure of union -> congenital Polycystic Kidney Disease. • WT1: Expressed by blastema; regulates GDNF synthesis.

• RET Receptor Tyrosine Kinase: Expressed at ureteric bud tips; binds GDNF to stimulate bud branching. • FGF2 & WNT4: Secreted by bud tips; prevents blastema apoptosis & induces Mesenchymal-to-Epithelial Transition (MET) to form S-shaped
• Ascent: Sacral S1 to Lumbar T12-L3 (weeks 6-9), driven by spinal elongation and reduction of fetal body curvature.

• Medial Rotation: 90° medial rotation brings hilum from ventral to anteromedial direction. • Sequential Revascularization: Lower transient aortic branches degenerate as new cranial branches form. Persistence of lower branches →> Accessory Renal Arteries (~25%), which can cross UPJ causing hydronephrosis. • Incidence & Fusion: 1 in 500; 95% fusion of lower poles across midline anterior to aorta (week 7 in pelvis).

• Arrest of Ascent: Central isthmus gets trapped beneath the root of the Inferior Mesenteric Artery (IMA) at L3 • Associations & Risks: Turner Syndrome (45,XO), Trisomies (13, 18, 21); predisposing to UPJ obstruction, stones, and recurrent UTIs. • Unilateral Agenesis: 1 in 1000; failure of ureteric bud sprouting; solitary kidney undergoes compensatory hypertrophy with normal lifespan.
• Bilateral Agenesis: 1 in 4000; complete absence of fetal urine -> Severe Oligohydramnios.

• Potter Sequence Triad: (1) Pulmonary Hypoplasia (primary cause of neonatal death), (2) Potter Facies (flat nose, micrognathia, low-set ears), (3) Limb deformities (clubbed feet). Incompatible with life.

**3 Successive Renal Systems**: • Pronephros: Early week 4 (cervical); completely non-functional in humans; full regression by end week 4. • Mesonephros: Late week 4-10 (thoracolumbar); produces primitive dilute urine; Wolffian duct persists in males (epididymis, vas deferens, ejaculatory duct, seminal vesicles). • Metanephros: Week 5 onward (sacral S1-S2); permanent kidney; urine filtration starts at Week 12. • Ureteric Bud (Collecting System): Outgrowth of caudal Wolffian duct -> Ureter, Renal Pelvis, Major Calyces (2-3), Minor Calyces (8-18),
